### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/meta (route, 51 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7a3f4e86e230dff87d3ff86eb6941b41907f8825` — the merge of head `340d02d8c0252a63a2778715bd240b5cec8df6a6` into base `1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7a3f4e86e230dff87d3ff86eb6941b41907f8825 && git checkout 7a3f4e86e230dff87d3ff86eb6941b41907f8825
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 340d02d8c0252a63a2778715bd240b5cec8df6a6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60 && git merge --no-ff 340d02d8c0252a63a2778715bd240b5cec8df6a6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1e65a389e12e7c07e2121378d1d0755226c2ad60` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `340d02d8c0252a63a2778715bd240b5cec8df6a6`

review (review-b, areas S2+S4) · 2026-11-15T11:18Z

I read the full diff at this head against GitHub: 8 files, +672/−30. I also read the three cards, the claims (6892161268 and its siblings), `ensureObjectStorage` on this tree, and `check-governed-merges --pr 33805`, which reports NOT governed at 702 lines.

### Correctness

1. **#33563, honest outcome: holds.**
   - `rowWritten` is set only after a row write lands. The removal limb sets it inside `if (current)`, and its projector call is gated on the same `current`, so a `failed[]` entry never reads "undefined".
   - `settle` routes any `notApplied` step to `failed[]`. The steps are:
     - the registry write-through's returned refusal, now read instead of discarded;
     - `ensureObjectStorage`'s advisory;
     - a projector answering `success: false`.
   - The `catch` prefixes the row state only when a row was written.
   - The revert commit is built from `revertPlan`, the rows the walk changed, so a row restored under a failed item is still on the append-only history.
   - The `success` rule ("true exactly when nothing failed") already follows `failed[]`.
   - Choosing "report in `failed[]`" over "weaken the docblock and ADR" keeps ADR-0067's promise and the method's own docblock. Neither is reinterpreted.
2. **#33564, revert of a revert: holds.**
   - `replacedVersion()` reads the committing package's active row, the same address and the same `typeof version === 'number'` reading as `publishPackageDrafts` (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts:1973`). It reads before each write on both limbs, inside the `try`, so a read fault fails the item with nothing written.
   - `existedBefore` is `current !== null` on both limbs:
     - a removed row's revert-of-revert restores it;
     - a row the restore wrote again is removed by the revert-of-revert.
   - A legacy item (`existedBefore` with no version) is named in `failed[]` with nothing written, with the history/rollback route as its remedy, instead of being skipped silently.
3. **#33486, docblock: holds.** The prose matches `recordPackageCommit`: best effort, and `revertCommitId` is omitted on failure. Blocker #33465 has merged.
4. **Pins and ablations.**
   - The new file's 10 cases assert the item's placement, the row state, `code` (`NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`) and the revert commit's items, not just `success`.
   - A1–A6 each map to a limb; A1's predicted 6 came out as 5, which is explained.
   - The two flipped pins (`prevVersion` null → 2, and the stored-expression revert now in `failed[]`) are the behaviour these cards correct, and both are named in the body.

### Scope and declarations

- **`Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are correct.**
  - There are no new exports, and no type or key moves. `failed[].code` was already optional and free-form, and no error code is coined.
  - A revert that used to answer `success: true` while the process had not acted on it now answers `false`. That brings the answer back to its declared contract; it neither widens nor narrows a published accept set.
- **Changeset.** `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. I checked each sentence against the diff, including the legacy-revert remedy route and the best-effort record.
- **File surface.** The claim names `protocol-package-commits.ts` and the `protocol.ts` docblocks. The objectql test double (`syncObjectSchema`), the flipped objectql pin and the three additive `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` rows are outside it; they are named in the body as seat-approved and are test or ledger only. `protocol.ts` changes docblock prose only. Not governed.
- **Card relation.** `Fixes #33563`, `Fixes #33564` and `Fixes #33486` are each correct; nothing remains on any of them.

### Nits (no change required)

1. **The storage step fails on more than a refused sync.** `ensureObjectStorage` also returns the column-changes-not-applied warning, and that fails the item too. The entry names the advisory's `rule`, so it is accurate. The body's "storage sync refused" undersells this; the changeset's "its storage not following the restored body" is correct.
2. **One extra read per item.** `replacedVersion()` reads the row `repo.get` just read as `current`.
3. **A no-op removal is still in the plan.** On the removal limb with no `current` row, `revertPlan` still records an item that changed no row (`existedBefore: false`). The earlier code did the same through `reverted[]`, so this is not a regression.

### Follow-ups, not part of this PR (for the seat)

- The ADR-0067 amendment's "What the doors do" text (11-14) now describes the code before this PR. A status-line amendment is owed, and it is governed (Tier H).
- `applyRegistryWriteThrough` (non-object types) and `restoreArtifactRegistryView` still only log their own faults. This is the body's loose end, shared with the save and publish doors.

### Check-runs at this head (read at review time)

- 16 `success`, including `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.
- 16 skipped.
- 16 still running: Build Core, Test Core 1–8/8, Type Check · workspace, consumer gates and debt ledger, three Lint jobs, and Live E2E UI. None had failed.
- Landing waits for every check on this head to be green or an expected skip.

**Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write).
